# [C4 — Baltic inflow events](../hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_c4.py`: what the data held here can and cannot show about the hypothesis. Each marked statement links to what it rests on.*

**Draft, not a result.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-STATUS">The test this page specifies has not been run: no script in this repository computes it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-STATUS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The observable consequence

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-ORDER">The falsifiable half of [C4](../hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events") is **ordered propagation**: a wind-forced inflow event at month τ produces a bottom-salinity anomaly whose **peak lag increases along the path** Belts/Øresund → Arkona → Bornholm → Gotland Deep, read there at [200](../SOURCES.md#F-9be4156372) m, the depth at which the published inflow statistics read the eastern Gotland Basin. The test is whether the peaks fall in that order.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-ORDER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-FALSIFY">**Falsified if** the peak lags are not in path order, or the Gotland salinity peak comes no later than the event month, or the ordering statistic — Kendall τ of peak lag against the sites' order along the path — lies inside the null below.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-FALSIFY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-SECONDARY">Secondary: an event should raise `sal_bed` more than `sal_surf`. If both rise alike, the salinity difference between bed and surface at the Danish stations does not grow, and the part of [C4](../hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events") that has the pulses strengthen stratification above them is not seen at the Danish end.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-SECONDARY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The data held

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-SERIES">`docs/data/areas/stations_series.{json,bin}`, the monthly panel: `sal_bed` on [83,309](../SOURCES.md#F-8a4e8ec0a0) station-months at [1,395](../SOURCES.md#F-f7bd812015) stations, `oxy_bed` on [76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-e4779c5760) at [1,327](../SOURCES.md#F-1766a595e3), `sal_surf` on [83,341](../SOURCES.md#F-3a60c33ffc); the `.bin` is exactly as long as the layout its `.json` declares.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-SERIES "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-BEDBIN">Each value is a station's monthly median, and `_bed` is the deepest quarter of each cast's depth range, so *near the bed* is a band whose depth changes from cast to cast; the extract behind it has no time of day.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-BEDBIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-FLAGS">The panel holds values no water can hold — the flag record marks the sign-inverted oxygen of May and June 2005 — so it is read with the flag record beside it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-FLAGS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-MAAL">`data/raw/oda/maaledybde.csv.gz` gives `BundDybde_m` per visit: [151,203](../SOURCES.md#F-5683df4d6c) records, with a bottom depth at [1,176](../SOURCES.md#F-b78e848332) stations.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-MAAL "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-MBIFILE">`data/raw/cmems/indicators/omi_health_tempsaloxy_baltic_mbi_bottom_salinity_arkona_bornholm_P20250527.nc` holds `sob_ark` and `sob_bor`, daily from 1993-01-01 to 2024-12-31 with no value missing. Its title reads *bottom salinity from Reanalysis* and its source is `BALTICSEA_MULTIYEAR_PHY_003_011`: **a model output, not an observation**.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-MBIFILE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-GOTFILE">`…_mbi_sto2tz_gotland_P20250527.nc` holds `so`, `to` and `oxy` against depth at the Gotland Deep, on a monthly step and a one-metre depth step; its title ends *from Observations Reprocessing*, and its comment says the measurements were regridded onto that grid, so fine vertical structure is interpolation between discrete samples. Salinity and temperature run from 1993-01 to 2024-11; oxygen, declared as a volume fraction in units of `0.001` (ml/l), fills [226](../SOURCES.md#F-e28b0c81f0) months from 2005-11 to 2025-01.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-GOTFILE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-WIND">`data/raw/marine/wind_baltic_n.json`, `_c` and `_s` each hold hourly `wind_speed_10m` (km/h) and `wind_direction_10m` from 1995-01-01T00:00 to 2025-12-31T23:00 with no value missing, each at one point; all three points lie east of Bornholm, so none is over the Kattegat or the Belts.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-WIND "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-WINDSRC">No script in this repository fetched them and `data/raw/` is not under version control, so what model or observation lies behind this wind is not recorded here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-WINDSRC "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**A trap in the files.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-FILL">Both netCDF files mark a missing cell with the fill value `1e36` (`_FillValue`); a reader that does not mask it averages fill into the result.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-FILL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-GOTUNITS">`docs/data/baltic/gotland.json`, the project's copy of the Gotland profiles, converts the oxygen from ml/l to mg/l and records the product as in-situ profiles regridded onto a grid, not a reanalysis.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-GOTUNITS "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-CHAIN">So the Gotland file is observation-derived and the Arkona and Bornholm file is not: the observations run from the Danish stations to the Gotland Deep, and `sob_ark` and `sob_bor` serve only as a model check.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-CHAIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The station panel

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-PANEL">**The rule.** Stations inside [10](../SOURCES.md#F-8d988c3666)–[15](../SOURCES.md#F-ff67d5d2a8) °E and [54](../SOURCES.md#F-a12a6c0f1a)–[56.5](../SOURCES.md#F-ae661b1220) °N whose median bottom depth is at least [20](../SOURCES.md#F-d213ba86e1) m and which carry at least [120](../SOURCES.md#F-d29c796283) monthly `sal_bed` medians in 1993–2024, each listed individually, never merged into a water body.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-PANEL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-PANEL-N">No script here applies the rule, so how many stations pass it, and in which months they were sampled, is not known.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-PANEL-N "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The event index

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-INDEX">Eastward wind at the southern point (`wind_baltic_s.json`), from speed and direction, as a daily mean; its [10](../SOURCES.md#F-eb88322a13)-day running sum is the westerly burst, multiplied by the easterly deficit of the [35](../SOURCES.md#F-1e328e10eb) days before it, with a gap of [5](../SOURCES.md#F-6270109e4e) days between them, as preconditioning. Winter maxima of the index give the event onsets.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-INDEX "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-INDEX-NORUN">No script here computes the index, so which winters it ranks highest is not known, and whether its maxima are the published inflow events can be checked only against the IOW record, which is not held.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-INDEX-NORUN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The null, under the constraint actually imposed

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-NULLRULE">Not the statistic's nominal null. Deep water in the central Baltic is renewed by major inflows and otherwise stagnates, so a Gotland deep series persists from one month to the next, and a threshold set for independent months is crossed more often than it allows. The null is computed on surrogates that keep the series' own persistence.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-NULLRULE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-N1">**`N1`, primary: circular shift of the event index by whole years**, over the years from 1995, when the wind begins, that the index and the responses share. Whole years keep event seasonality, any seasonal pattern of sampling and every series' autocorrelation; only the alignment dies. The smallest p it can give is one over the number of alignments, the true one included — state it, never exceed it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-N1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-N2">**`N2`: [10,000](../SOURCES.md#F-b6d8ac2b3c) amplitude-adjusted phase-randomised surrogates** of each response.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-N2 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-RP">Random phases keep a series' periodogram, its linear correlation; the amplitude-adjusted version (AAFT) tries to keep its distribution of values as well.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-RP "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-BOUND">`N1` and `N2` bound the answer from two sides; take the more conservative.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-BOUND "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-PANELNULL">**The panel's stations are not replicates.** Neighbouring positions sampled in the same months can see the same water, so the statistic is the median across positions of a per-station z-anomaly, the panel shifts as one, and the null is over **time only**: spread across stations buys precision, not degrees of freedom. The sensitivity run is one fit per station, reported as a *distribution of lags*, not as separate tests. If only the composite shows the signal, the composite made it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-PANELNULL "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Procedure

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-P1">Build the wind index above; take its winter maxima and the top *k* onsets, for k = [3](../SOURCES.md#F-91ed13ae96), [5](../SOURCES.md#F-16daf10c54) and [8](../SOURCES.md#F-f37c341d77), declared before seeing the answer.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-P1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-P2">Per station, subtract that station's **own** month-of-year median from `sal_bed`, `sal_surf` and `oxy_bed`; divide by its interquartile range. Never pool before de-seasoning.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-P2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-P3">Same for `sob_ark` and `sob_bor` as monthly means, and for the Gotland `so` and `oxy` at [200](../SOURCES.md#F-9be4156372) m, after masking the fill value, in the file's own units.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-P3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
4. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-P4">Superposed-epoch composite at lags from −[12](../SOURCES.md#F-55ed2e801b) to +[24](../SOURCES.md#F-255eb2999d) months per site; record the peak lag.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-P4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
5. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-P5">Statistic: Kendall τ of peak lag against the sites' order along the path — Belts, Arkona, Bornholm, Gotland. τ depends only on ranks, so the order gives the same statistic as any distances that keep it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-P5 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
6. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-P6">Recompute τ under `N1` and `N2`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-P6 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
7. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-P7">Secondary: the same on `sal_bed − sal_surf`; and a check on `oxy_bed` for a rise followed by a fall — the pulse ventilating, then stratifying.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-P7 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What a result would and would not license

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-WOULD">**Would.** A clean falsification if the order breaks — cheap, and robust to any error that shifts or rescales a series without moving when its peak falls, because τ uses only the order of the peak lags. Otherwise weak corroboration, capped at `N1`'s p floor.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-WOULD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Would not.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-NOT-N">(a) The effective sample is the number of inflow events, not the number of months, so no effect size is estimable; and the Gotland oxygen record begins in 2005-11, so the oxygen limb sees only the events after that — how many, the published chronology would say.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-NOT-N "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-NOT-O1">(b) Nothing about [C4](../hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events")'s contribution to **[O1](../HYPOTHESES.md "Oxygen deficit")** in Danish water: the design follows salinity along the path toward the Gotland Deep and has no step from there to oxygen at Danish stations.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-NOT-O1 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-NOT-EXO">(c) It does not test *entirely exogenous to Danish policy*: exogeneity of the wind is assumed, and exogeneity of the consequences is a different claim.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-NOT-EXO "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE">(d) `sal_bed`, `temp_bed` and `oxysat_bed` come from the same CTD casts; salinity is estimated from conductivity, and saturation is oxygen as a share of what water holds at its temperature and salinity: they are **one** piece of evidence, not three.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-NOT-THREE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-CC-C4-NEXT">**Smallest improvement:** fetch the IOW Major Baltic Inflow statistics, replacing a self-built proxy with the published chronology [C4](../hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events") names.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-CC-C4-NEXT "What this claim rests on")</sup>
